palette: Bleached white marble and hyper-saturated Gulf blue sky — the specific noon quality of UAE light where every surface either blinds or retreats into hard shadow. Warm amber-sand in the shade pockets between towers. Cool cyan-silver in the glass reflections. Deep obsidian in the undersides of architectural overhangs.
lighting: Brutal vertical noon sun at 42°C. No golden hour. No diffusion. Hard 90-degree shadows cut across marble plazas like surgical incisions. Interior AC creates visible temperature haze at the threshold between inside and outside. Glass towers act as mirrors, doubling and tripling the light.
material_friction: Polished cream-and-grey Italian marble (lobby tiles, massive grid joints), floor-to-ceiling tempered glass facades (infinite city reflections), brushed aluminum door frames and elevator tracks, fine desert sand accumulated at the base of walls and along baseboard seams despite best efforts, black neoprene laptop bags piled near co-working tables.
instagram_prompts: First-person perspective (FPP) optic sensor capture from nanobot position at base of a glass tower in Dubai Media City, UAE. Wide-angle 14mm. Looking straight up the facade of a mirror-glass skyscraper — the tower stretches impossibly high, its surface reflecting a perfect duplicate of the neighboring tower creating recursive infinite geometry. Brutal vertical noon sun cuts a blinding white seam down the center of the frame. The marble plaza beneath occupies the extreme foreground in sharp detail — each tile joint enormous, dust motes settled in the grooves, a crushed coffee cup near the baseboard. Deep shadows cut at perfect right angles. Bleached white and hyper-blue Gulf sky above. Warm sand-amber in the shadow zones. A band of crawling traffic visible at street level before the towers claim the frame. No humans visible, no robots, no mechanical elements. World feels enormous, observer feels microscale. 4K photorealistic, neo-cyberpunk, technically precise.

First-person perspective (FPP) optic sensor capture from nanobot position skimming across the polished marble lobby floor of Media One Hotel, Dubai Media City. Wide-angle 14mm, deep focus, extreme low angle. The marble tile surface dominates the immediate foreground — cool grey-cream stone, enormous, each vein and inclusion visible in high detail, tile grout lines receding in sharp perspective toward a distant reception desk. Human legs and wheeled suitcases stand enormous in the mid-ground, proportionally immense. The glass front doors are visible in the background — through them, the exterior glare is blinding white against the cool interior. Bleached interior lighting. A scuffed sneaker sole detail in the foreground. No faces, no robots. Mood: precise, observational, alien-scale. 4K photorealistic, neo-cyberpunk.

First-person perspective (FPP) optic sensor capture from nanobot position on a rooftop terrace table surface, Media One Hotel Dubai, late afternoon. Wide-angle 14mm, extremely close to the table surface. The immediate foreground: a glass of water condensating heavily in the heat, an open laptop, a stack of printed research pages with dense text visible but microscale, a pen. The scene beyond: Sheikh Zayed Road visible far below, the Dubai Media City tower cluster in the mid-distance — glass facades catching the low amber sun, one tower still in harsh daylight, the adjacent tower already in deep blue shadow. The Gulf of Arabia glimmers on the far horizon through golden haze. The sky is hyper-saturated blue fading toward amber at the horizon. No people, no robots, no overlays. World is enormous, observer is microscale. 4K photorealistic, neo-cyberpunk, precise.
